bugs.error_message: test grammar_escapes_quotes_in_names FAILED - GBNF terminal emitted `"we"ird"`, inner quote unescaped
bugs.root_cause: gbnf_json_string escaped only ONE layer. Two stack: the model emits JSON (a `"` in a name arrives as `\"`), and GBNF terminals are themselves double-quoted, so that backslash AND that quote each need a further GBNF escape. Single-layer escaping lets a quote close the terminal early and corrupts every rule after it.
bugs.fix: Serialise with serde_json::to_string first (JSON layer), then escape backslashes then quotes for the GBNF layer. A name containing `"` now renders as `\\\"` in the grammar.

bugs.error_message: duplicate values in JSON-schema `enum` for peer/capability (found by review, not by a failing test)
bugs.root_cause: Used Vec::dedup() on the peer list. Vec::dedup only removes CONSECUTIVE duplicates. The list is deduped by (peer,capability) PAIR, so a peer exposing several caps repeats non-consecutively and survived.
bugs.fix: Added unique_in_order(): HashSet-based dedup preserving first-seen order, applied to both peer and capability enums. Added test json_schema_enums_have_no_duplicates with a peer exposing 2 caps and a cap name shared by 2 peers.

bugs.error_message: Capability output blobs never appear in the Files panel (Inbound category always empty)
bugs.root_cause: record_inbound_output indexed downloaded output blobs with local_user_id=None and client_id=None, while storage::blobs::list_user_visible selects on `local_user_id = ?1 OR client_id = ?2`. Two NULLs match neither branch, so every user_visible output row was unreachable: stored, GC-counted, invisible. No owner context was threaded from the planner down to the blob index.
bugs.fix: Added BlobOwner {client_id, conversation_id}, built from ConversationState in plan_exec.rs and threaded through execute_plan_streaming -> fetch_output_blobs -> record_inbound_output. Also sets capability and a derived provisional path. Regression test crates/server/tests/blob_outputs.rs, verified to fail against the old code.

bugs.error_message: Planner fabricates a completed action when the user message contains no request ("Je vous ai ouvert le fichier ... sur votre appareil")
bugs.root_cause: A message made only of @ mentions scopes the catalogue but asks nothing. The reflect system prompt opens with 'The user asked a question and a plan was executed; you now have the blackboard', which presupposes both. With an empty plan and an empty blackboard the model filled the blank from the conversation tail and reported having opened a file attached in an earlier turn. The existing honesty rule only covered 'the user asked for a side effect and no tool did it' — not 'the user asked for nothing and you invented both request and action'.
bugs.fix: mention::is_scope_only/strip_mentions detect a mention-only message; reflect_only then injects a system line saying there is no request, do not guess, do not claim anything was done. Reflect prompt also gained a general rule: the blackboard is the complete record, the composer performs no action itself and must never claim one. Verified against qwen2.5:7b on a live node: the same message now answers 'Je n'ai pas de contexte sur cette mention. Pouvez-vous me dire ce que vous souhaitez faire ?'

bugs.error_message: Reflect retypes tool outputs instead of quoting them: reply showed 'Z29601:06:08-12-09-2026' where reverse had returned 'Z706178087.92:60:81T21-90-6202'
bugs.root_cause: blackboard_summary renders '- peer::capability -> value' with no step id, so the composer has no handle for a value and can only retype it. A 7B asked to state a reversed string re-derives the reversal in its head and gets it wrong; a short number beside it (char count) is copied correctly, which is why only long opaque strings drift. Observed with 9-digit nanosecond timestamps on Linux (30 chars); not reproduced on macOS where timestamps are 27 chars.
bugs.fix: referenceable_values() lists '${step.field} = value' tokens in the reflect prompt, the prompt instructs the composer to write the reference rather than the value, and resolve_value substitutes them in the returned reply. Unresolvable references degrade to visible text. Mechanism unit-tested; the end-to-end symptom was not reproducible locally.

bugs.error_message: A ToolCall could be persisted without its ToolResult: persist_tool_pair_at wrote the pair in two separate transactions
bugs.root_cause: persist_tool_pair_at looped over (call, result) calling conversations::append_turn once each, and append_turn opens its own transaction. If the second insert failed — a seq collision, a lock, a disk error — the call stayed committed. The reloaded conversation then showed an invocation that never returned, and the planner's context gained a question with no answer. The executor's hook only logs the error, so execution continued.
bugs.fix: Added conversations::append_turns writing every turn in one transaction; append_turn is now a one-element wrapper. persist_tool_pair_at builds both records then writes them together. Regression test squats the result's seq to force the second insert to fail and asserts nothing is left behind — verified to fail against the old code (3 turns instead of 2).
